goal.en: Spot the second reading of your own sentence before a reader does — and know when to keep it.
goal.ar: أن تلمح القراءة الثانية لجملتك قبل أن يلمحها القارئ، وأن تعرف متى تُبقيها.

head: Sentence
Second reading
rows: We discussed the plan to close the site.
we discussed it in order to close the site
She saw the man with the telescope.
the man was holding the telescope
Visiting relatives can be tiring.
relatives who visit are tiring
He told her he had lied on Tuesday.
the lie happened on Tuesday
The report criticises the manager and the auditor.
one criticism, two targets — or two reports?

text.en: Ambiguity almost always comes from attachment: which word does this phrase belong to? The cure is to move the phrase, not to add words.
text.ar: ينشأ اللبس غالباً من الارتباط: بأي كلمة تتصل هذه العبارة؟ والعلاج نقل العبارة لا إضافة كلمات.

text.en: You cannot detect this by rereading your own sentence — you already know what you meant. Read it looking deliberately for the wrong meaning.
text.ar: لن تكتشف هذا بإعادة قراءة جملتك، فأنت تعرف مرادك سلفاً. اقرأها متعمّداً البحث عن المعنى الخاطئ.

head: Position of only
Meaning
rows: Only I told him the truth.
nobody else told him
I only told him the truth.
I did nothing else, or told nobody else
I told only him the truth.
I told nobody else
I told him only the truth.
I said nothing false

text.en: “Only” attaches to whatever follows it. In speech, stress fixes the meaning; in writing, position is all you have.
text.ar: ترتبط only بما يليها. وفي الكلام تحدّد النبرةُ المعنى، أما في الكتابة فليس لديك سوى الموضع.

text.en: Negation has the same problem. “All that glitters is not gold” is understood, but it literally says nothing that glitters is gold. Convention rescues the proverb; it will not rescue your report.
text.ar: وللنفي المشكلة نفسها. فجملة All that glitters is not gold مفهومة، لكنها حرفياً تعني أن لا شيء لامع ذهب. والعرف ينقذ المثل، ولن ينقذ تقريرك.

head: Context
Ambiguity is
rows: a contract or a safety notice
a defect to be removed
a diplomatic communiqué
a tool for agreeing without agreeing
a job reference
a way to warn without writing it
a joke
the mechanism itself
a poem or a headline
a way to hold two meanings at once

text.en: The question is never whether a sentence is ambiguous, but whether you chose the ambiguity. Unchosen ambiguity is always a fault.
text.ar: السؤال ليس أفي الجملة لبس، بل أأنت اخترت هذا اللبس. فاللبس غير المختار عيبٌ دائماً.

text.en: “We agree on the need for further discussion” commits both sides to nothing. That is not sloppy writing; it is precisely engineered.
text.ar: عبارة «نتفق على الحاجة إلى مزيد من النقاش» لا تُلزم أحداً بشيء، وليست كتابة رخوة بل هندسة دقيقة.

prompt.en: “She saw the man with the telescope.” What is the second reading?

options: The man was carrying the telescope.
She used a telescope to see the man.
The man was standing near a telescope.
She bought a telescope from the man.

explanation.en: “With the telescope” can attach to “saw” or to “the man” — classic attachment ambiguity.
explanation.ar: عبارة with the telescope قد تتصل بالفعل saw أو بالاسم the man، وهو لبس ارتباط كلاسيكي.

prompt.en: Which sentence is ambiguous in a way the writer probably did not intend?
prompt.ar: أي جملة فيها لبس لم يقصده الكاتب على الأرجح؟

options: The board discussed the plan to close the northern site.
The board met to discuss closing the northern site.
The board discussed a proposal for closing the site.
The board considered whether to close the northern site.

explanation.en: It can mean they discussed a closure plan, or met in order to close the site. The others fix the reading.
explanation.ar: قد تعني أنهم ناقشوا خطة الإغلاق، أو أنهم اجتمعوا كي يُغلقوا الموقع. والبقية تُثبّت المعنى.

prompt.en: How do you fix “He told her he had lied on Tuesday”?

options: Move the time phrase: “On Tuesday he told her he had lied.”
Add a comma: “He told her, he had lied on Tuesday.”
Change the tense: “He tells her he lied on Tuesday.”
Add a word: “He definitely told her he had lied on Tuesday.”

explanation.en: Ambiguity of attachment is cured by moving the phrase, not by punctuation or emphasis.
explanation.ar: لبس الارتباط يُعالَج بنقل العبارة لا بعلامات الترقيم ولا بالتوكيد.

prompt.en: “Visiting relatives can be tiring.” Which pair of readings is right?
prompt.ar: أي زوج من القراءات صحيح لهذه الجملة؟

options: Going to see them is tiring / they are tiring when they visit.
They are always tiring / they are never tiring at all.
They travel a long way / they arrive without warning.
They are tired themselves / they make the journey often.

explanation.en: “Visiting” can be a gerund (the act) or a participle modifying “relatives” (the people).
explanation.ar: كلمة visiting قد تكون مصدراً يدل على الفعل، أو اسم فاعل يصف relatives أي الأشخاص.

prompt.en: Which sentence means “I said nothing false to him”?
prompt.ar: أي جملة تعني «لم أقل له شيئاً كاذباً»؟

options: I told him only the truth.
Only I told him the truth.
I only told him the truth.
I told only him the truth.

explanation.en: “Only” attaches to what follows it, so it must sit directly before “the truth”.
explanation.ar: ترتبط only بما يليها، فيجب أن تسبق the truth مباشرة.

prompt.en: Which sentence means “nobody else told him”?
prompt.ar: أي جملة تعني «لم يخبره أحد غيري»؟

options: Only I told him the truth.
I told him only the truth.
I only told him the truth.
I told the truth only to him.

explanation.en: Placing “only” before “I” restricts the subject rather than the object or the action.
explanation.ar: وضع only قبل I يقصر الحصر على الفاعل لا على المفعول ولا على الفعل.

prompt.en: “All that glitters is not gold.” What is the literal reading?

options: Nothing that glitters is gold.
Some glittering things are not gold.
Everything that is gold glitters.
Gold is the only thing that glitters.

explanation.en: The negation scopes over “all”. Convention gives us the intended sense; the grammar does not.
explanation.ar: النفي هنا يشمل all. والعرف هو الذي يمنحنا المعنى المقصود، لا القواعد.

prompt.en: Which version states the intended meaning unambiguously?
prompt.ar: أي صيغة تذكر المعنى المقصود بلا لبس؟

options: Not everything that glitters is gold.
All that glitters is not gold at all.
Nothing that glitters is really gold.
Everything glittering may not be gold.

explanation.en: Moving the negation in front of “everything” makes the scope explicit.
explanation.ar: تقديم النفي على everything يجعل مدى النفي صريحاً.

prompt.en: Match each placement of “only” with its meaning.
prompt.ar: صِل كل موضع لكلمة only بمعناه.

pairs: I told him only the truth.
I did nothing more than tell

explanation.en: Four positions, four meanings — and in writing, position is the only signal you have.
explanation.ar: أربعة مواضع بأربعة معانٍ، وفي الكتابة لا إشارة لديك سوى الموضع.

prompt.en: Two governments announce: “We agree on the need for further discussion.” What has been agreed?
prompt.ar: أعلنت حكومتان: «نتفق على الحاجة إلى مزيد من النقاش». على ماذا اتُّفق؟

options: Nothing of substance; only that talking will continue.
A detailed timetable for resolving the dispute.
That one side has accepted the other's position.
That the discussions have now been concluded.

explanation.en: The sentence is engineered to let both sides sign it. That is diplomacy, not vagueness.
explanation.ar: صيغت الجملة لتمكّن الطرفين من التوقيع عليها، وهذه دبلوماسية لا غموض.

prompt.en: In which context is ambiguity always a defect?
prompt.ar: في أي سياق يكون اللبس عيباً دائماً؟

options: A safety instruction on a machine.
A newspaper headline about a scandal.
A poem about a childhood memory.
A joke told among close friends.

explanation.en: Where a misreading has physical consequences, a second meaning is a hazard, not a texture.
explanation.ar: حيث تكون لسوء الفهم عواقب مادية، يصير المعنى الثاني خطراً لا ثراءً.

prompt.en: A reference says: “You would be lucky to get him to work for you.” Why is this dangerous to write?
prompt.ar: لماذا تُعدّ هذه الجملة خطرة في خطاب تزكية؟

options: It can be read as high praise or as a warning.
It uses a conditional where a past tense is needed.
It is far too informal for a written reference.
It names the candidate directly rather than by role.

explanation.en: “Lucky to get him to work” — fortunate to employ him, or unlikely to get any work out of him.
explanation.ar: قد تعني أنك محظوظ بتوظيفه، وقد تعني أنك بالكاد ستنتزع منه عملاً.

prompt.en: Which sentence has only one possible reading?
prompt.ar: أي جملة لا تحتمل إلا قراءة واحدة؟

options: Using a telescope, she saw the man on the hill.
She saw the man on the hill with the telescope.
She saw with the telescope the man on the hill.
The man on the hill with the telescope was seen.

explanation.en: Fronting the participle clause fixes the instrument to the seeing and leaves nothing to attach elsewhere.
explanation.ar: تقديم جملة اسم الفاعل يربط الأداة بفعل الرؤية ولا يترك ما يتصل بغيره.

prompt.en: Remove the ambiguity by moving one phrase: “He told her he had resigned on Friday.” Begin: “On Friday ___”
prompt.ar: أزل اللبس بنقل عبارة واحدة، وابدأ بـ On Friday

questions.answer: he told her he had resigned

explanation.en: Fronting the time phrase attaches it to the telling, which is presumably what was meant.
explanation.ar: تقديم عبارة الزمن يربطها بفعل الإخبار، وهو المقصود على الأرجح.

prompt.en: You are drafting a safety notice. Which version is right?
prompt.ar: تكتب لافتة سلامة. أي صيغة صحيحة؟

options: Do not operate this machine unless a supervisor is present.
Do not operate this machine without supervision being present.
This machine should not be operated when unsupervised by staff.
Operating this machine unsupervised is not to be undertaken.

explanation.en: Short, active, one reading. On a safety notice, elegance is worth nothing and clarity is worth everything.
explanation.ar: قصيرة ومبنية للمعلوم وبقراءة واحدة. وعلى لافتة السلامة لا قيمة للأناقة، والقيمة كلها للوضوح.
